entries.description: (manager): reads sos\melodic.bnk, sos\drum.bnk and sos\drum32.dig whole through the manager's volume stream +0x504 (VolRStream_Open, VolRStream_GetSize, operator new, the stream's read slot +0x1c, VolRStream_Close) and keeps far pointers to them at +0x13a, +0x146 and +0x140; returns 1, or 0 at the first that fails to open, allocate or read.

entries.name: SoundManager_SetSampleNames
entries.description: (manager, names): keeps the null-terminated array of name pointers at +0x508. For each name, an empty one gets size 0; any other is opened through the volume stream +0x504 and its VolRStream_GetSize stored at +0x262[i], and the function returns at once when it fails to open. Each name's data far pointer +0x38e[i] and reference count byte +0x352[i] are cleared. After the last it sets the highest name index +0x502 to the count less one.

entries.name: SoundManager_SetSampleName
entries.description: (manager, index, name) in stack order: returns 0 for no name, an index above +0x502, or a name in which Str_FindBoyerMoore over 0006f948's result finds none of .sfx and .raw (kind 0) and .hmp (kind 1). Every object of the 60 slots on that index must be of that kind (byte +0x17), else it returns 0; each is stopped through its slot +0x14, unloaded by 00050164, has bit 1 of its flags +0xd set and bit 0 cleared, and takes the name. Then stores the name at +0x508[index], opens it through the stream +0x504, stores VolRStream_GetSize at +0x262[index], clears the data far pointer +0x38e[index] and returns 1; 0 when it fails to open.

entries.name: SoundObject_SetPosition
entries.description: (object, point) in stack order, callee-cleaned: sets the positional byte +0x15, copies the point's three ints to +0x25, +0x29 and +0x2d, and calls 0004fdd8(the manager +0x11, the channel byte +8).

entries.name: SoundObject_LoadSample
entries.description: (object), callee-cleaned: brings a sound object's sample into memory. Returns 0 unless bit 1 of the flags +0xd is set, and 1 at once when bit 0 (loaded) is. When the manager's (+0x11) bytes in use +0x4f6 plus the sample's size (manager +0x262 indexed by the object's +9) would pass the limit +0x4fe, it returns 0 unless the manager's byte +0x503 is set, and otherwise unloads (00050164), one at a time until the sample fits, the loaded object among the manager's 0x3c at +0x14c whose non-zero priority byte +0x34 is highest and at least this object's own, ties going to the larger size, and for which its vtable +0x30 returns 0; it returns 0 when none qualifies. It then allocates the size, reads the sample through the manager's volume stream +0x504 (VolRStream_Open with the object's name at +0, the stream's vtable +0x1c), stores the block's far pointer in the manager's 6-byte slot +0x38e, counts a reference in the byte +0x352 (adding the size to +0x4f6 on the first and raising the high-water mark +0x4fa), sets bit 0 of +0xd and returns 1.

entries.name: MidiSound_Ctor
entries.description: (memory or 0, slot, index, name, manager) in stack order: allocates 0xcf bytes when given none, runs 00050020 on the object, sets the vtable +0x3b to 00095c82 and the 32 dwords of the track map +0x3f to 0xff, the name +0, the index +9, the manager +0x11, the kind byte +0x17 to 1 and the slot byte +8; the flags +0xd are 2 with a name, else 0. Returns the object.

entries.name: MidiSound_Play
entries.description: (sound), slot +0x10 of vtable 00095c82: returns 0 when its slot +0x30 returns non-zero or SoundObject_LoadSample fails. Stores the far pointer to the loaded file (manager +0x38e for the index) at +0xbf and the far callback 0004e7b4 at +0xc7, and calls HmiMidi_InitSong (0006e4c1)(+0xbf, the track map +0x3f, the handle +0x19). A non-zero result goes to +4, is formatted as 'SoundObject::playMIDI: %s' with 0006f23d's text, sets +0x19 to -1 and the word +0x1d to 0xffff, and returns 0. Otherwise calls 0006eeae(handle, +0x35, word +0x39) when the far pointer +0x35 is set, then 0006ea6b(handle), copies the handle to the word +0x1d and the word +0x21 to +0x23, calls 0006ee87(handle, far 0004e718) and returns 1.

entries.name: DigiSound_Ctor
entries.description: (memory or 0, slot, index, name, manager) in stack order: allocates 0x50 bytes when given none, runs 00050020 on the object, sets the vtable +0x3b to 00095cd6, the name +0, the manager +0x11, the index +9, the slot byte +8, +0x3f to 2, the bytes +0x47 and the kind +0x17 to 0, and +0x48 and +0x4c to -1; the flags +0xd are 2 with a name, else 0. Returns the object.

entries.name: DigiSound_Dtor
entries.description: (sound, flags), slot +0x08 of vtable 00095cd6: unless null, resets the vtable to 00095cd6, stops it with DigiSound_Stop (00050c88), calls 000500d8(sound, 0), and frees it with operator delete when bit 0 of flags is set.

entries.name: DigiSound_Play
entries.description: (sound), slot +0x10 of vtable 00095cd6. When 0006e055(000bd8c8) is above 30, picks among the 60 objects (SoundManager_GetObject on 000bd73e) the digital one (+0x17 clear) whose slot +0x30 returns non-zero with the lowest 0005049c value below 100, and stops it through its slot +0x14; returns 0 with none. Returns 0 when SoundObject_LoadSample fails. The volume is byte +0x31 * 0x7fff * the manager's byte +0x241 / 10000, or the word +0x32 when the positional byte +0x15 is set; at volume 0 with +0x18 clear it returns 1. Otherwise builds a start block: the data far pointer (manager +0x38e for the index), its size +0x262 as the length at +8, the word +0x21 at +0xc (also copied to +0x23), +0x3f at +0x10, the volume at +0x14, 0x1000 + the slot byte +8 at +0x18, the far callback 0004e7fc at +0x1c, flags 0x4100 at +0x28 (0x4300 with +0x1f at +0x40 when positional), +0x43 at +0x38 when +0x47 is set, and with +0x21 non-zero and neither +0x48 nor +0x4c -1 those two at +0x30 and +0x34 and the flags' low byte 0x40. Stores the slot in the word +0x1d and HmiDigi_StartSample (0006dad9)(000bd8c8, block) in +0x19; on -1 sets +4 and +0x19 to -1 and +0x1d to 0xffff and returns 0; else returns 1.

entries.name: DigiSound_Stop
entries.description: (sound), slot +0x14 of vtable 00095cd6: when the voice +0x19 is not -1, calls 0006dd7f(000bd8c8, voice), then sets +0x19 to -1 and the word +0x1d to 0xffff.

entries.name: VGA8_SetSourcePage
entries.description: (page), C convention: the VGA_8 driver's slot 16 (table 000a7b70 +0x40): stores page at 00098dd6, its plane offset (0009e5ce + 4*page) at 0009e600 and its pan byte (0009e5f6 + page) shifted right 1 at 0009e60c. ES1GO's VGA8_SetSourcePage with the store of the page added.

entries.name: VGA8_SetDrawPage
entries.description: (page), C convention: the VGA_8 driver's slot 17: VGA8_SetSourcePage (00052644) into 00098dda, 0009e604 and 0009e610, the draw page.

entries.name: TSPartBase_FindPart
entries.description: (part, id) in stack order, callee-cleaned: returns part when its id number (+6) equals id, else 0. Slot +0x24 of TSPartBase's vtables and of the other vtables es1_naming.py vtables lists with it, 104 in all. ES2's TSPartBase_FindPart (DBSIM 00476120).

entries.name: TSPartBase_FindPartSlot
entries.description: (part, id), callee-cleaned, no frame: returns 0 (xor eax, eax; ret 8). Slot +0x28 of the vtables holding TSPartBase_FindPart. ES2's TSPartBase_FindPartSlot (DBSIM 00476134).

entries.name: TSPartList_Ctor
entries.description: (list), callee-cleaned: allocates 0x16 bytes when list is null and returns null when that fails; stores the vtables 000960a6, 000960ca (TSBase's) and 000960f6 (TSPartBase's) and then TSPartList's 0009612a, and clears the child count +0x10 (word) and the pointer array +0x12 (dword); returns list. ES2's TSPartList_Ctor (DBSIM 00476604).

entries.name: TSPartBase_DtorCopy
entries.description: (part, flags), callee-cleaned: TSPartBase_Dtor (0005d614)'s code with TSPartBase's second vtable 000960f6, whose slot +0x1c holds it: stores that vtable, runs TSBase_Dtor(part, 0) and calls operator_delete on part when flags bit 0 is set; returns at once for a null part. TSPartList_Ctor (00052cc0) installs 000960f6. ES2's TSPartBase_Dtor (DBSIM 0049224b).

entries.name: TSPartList_Dtor
entries.description: (list, flags), callee-cleaned: slot +0x1c of TSPartList's vtable 0009612a. Returns at once for a null list; otherwise stores that vtable, calls each non-null child's destructor slot (+0x1c) with flags 3, operator_delete on the pointer array +0x12, stores TSPartBase's vtable 000960f6, runs TSBase_Dtor(list, 0) and calls operator_delete on list when flags bit 0 is set. ES2's TSPartList_Dtor (DBSIM 00476648).

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Ctor
entries.description: (part), callee-cleaned: allocates 0x1a bytes when part is null and returns null when that fails; runs TSPartList_Ctor, stores TSDetailPart's vtable 00096162 and clears the threshold pointer +0x16; returns part. ES2's TSDetailPart_Ctor (DBSIM 00476834).

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Dtor
entries.description: (part, flags), callee-cleaned: slot +0x1c of TSDetailPart's vtable 00096162. Returns at once for a null part; otherwise stores that vtable, calls operator_delete on the thresholds +0x16, runs TSPartList_Dtor(part, 0) and calls operator_delete on part when flags bit 0 is set. ES2's TSDetailPart_Dtor (DBSIM 0047685c).

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Ctor
entries.description: (part), callee-cleaned: allocates 0x20 bytes when part is null and returns null when that fails; runs TSPartList_Ctor, stores TSBSPPart's vtable 00096196, and clears the node count +0x16 (word) and the node and transform-id pointers +0x18 and +0x1c; returns part. ES2's TSBSPPart_Ctor (DBSIM 004769a0).

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Dtor
entries.description: (part, flags), callee-cleaned: slot +0x1c of TSBSPPart's vtable 00096196. Returns at once for a null part; otherwise stores that vtable, calls __vec_delete(0, 0xe, 7, nodes +0x18), which with no destructor and flags bit 0 set calls operator_delete on the address 4 bytes before the nodes, calls operator_delete on the transform ids +0x1c, runs TSPartList_Dtor(part, 0) and calls operator_delete on part when flags bit 0 is set. ES2's TSBSPPart_Dtor (DBSIM 004769d4) frees the nodes with Mem_DeleteArray.

entries.name: VGA8_FillBitmapPolygon
entries.description: (count, points), C convention: the VGA_8 driver's table +0x84 (0009df58), which Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch calls for brush modes 5 and 7. Reads the brush at the clip block's (00098d64) +0x228: +8 the int32 {u, v} texture points, +0xc the bitmap header, +0x10 the colour table only for mode 7 (0 otherwise). Nothing for fewer than 3 points, a polygon with no height or no width, or one wholly outside the clip rect +0x20c..+0x218; one whose smallest y is above the rect's top is cut there with VGA8_BitmapPolyClipTop into 000b56d0/000b57d4 and redone. Walks by columns when the clip mode +0x204 is not 2 (edges from the first leftmost vertex, A forward and B backward, VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupColumns/StepColumns, x in 000bd950, VGA8_SpanBitmapColumn per column from the rect's left) and by rows when it is 2 (from the first topmost vertex, A backward and B forward, the Rows pair, y in 000bd94c, VGA8_SpanBitmapRow from the rect's top); stops when either edge ends at the far vertex, past the rect's far side, or when A's other coordinate exceeds B's, so the far vertex's column or row is never drawn. ES2's Raster_FillBitmapPolygon (DBSIM 0048a818) walks rows only.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 000534ac (mode test 0005350b, clip and walk loops 00053610-0005385d); driver table 000a7b70 +0x84 read from the image

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapPolyPointCtor
entries.description: (p), callee-cleaned: the empty constructor of an 8-byte int32 point, allocating 8 bytes when p is null; VGA8_FillBitmapPolygon's element constructor for its two 32-point clip buffers 000b56d0 and 000b57d4, built on first use (flags 000b56cc, 000b57d0).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00053864 and its __vec_ctor calls in 000534ac

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapPolyClipTop
entries.description: (top, texOut, pointsOut, countOut, texIn, pointsIn, countIn) in stack order, callee-cleaned: cuts a polygon and its texture points at y = top, keeping y >= top. Walking the ring from vertex 0, emits each vertex with y >= top and, when the edge to the next vertex crosses, the crossing c = c_i + (top - y_i) * (c_n - c_i) / (y_n - y_i) for each of x, u and v, from the vertex the edge leaves, the division truncating; the new count goes to countOut.

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapEdgeStepRows
entries.description: (edge), callee-cleaned: steps a row-walk edge of VGA8_FillBitmapPolygon one row: decrements +4 and at 0 starts the next edge from vertex +8 with VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupRows, returning 0 when that fails; otherwise adds +0x14 to u +0xc, +0x18 to v +0x10, +0x20 to x +0x1c, +0x2c to the error +0x28 and, when the error is positive, +0x24 (+-1) to x and subtracts +0x30. Returns 1. ES2's Raster_BitmapEdgeStep (DBSIM 0048a944).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 000539e4; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a944

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapEdgeStepColumns
entries.description: (edge), callee-cleaned: VGA8_BitmapEdgeStepRows for a column-walk edge, starting the next edge with VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupColumns; +0x1c is then the edge's y.

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupRows
entries.description: (vertex, edge), callee-cleaned: starts a row-walk edge of VGA8_FillBitmapPolygon from vertex: steps the index by the edge's +0 (+-1, wrapping round the count 000b56c0) past vertices with the same y, and returns 0 on reaching the far vertex 000b56bc. Otherwise stores the row count dy at +4, the next vertex at +8, u and v (texture point << 16) at +0xc/+0x10 and their steps Math_Q16Divide(du << 16, dy << 16) at +0x14/+0x18, x at +0x1c, its whole step dx / dy at +0x20, the +-1 carry at +0x24, the error at +0x28 (0, or 1 - dy for a leftward edge), the remainder |dx| % dy at +0x2c and dy at +0x30, so step k's x is x0 + ceil(k * dx / dy); returns 1. ES2's Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup (DBSIM 0048a9a0).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00053a94; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a9a0

entries.name: VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupColumns
entries.description: (vertex, edge), callee-cleaned: VGA8_BitmapEdgeSetupRows with x and y exchanged: the count is the vertices' x difference, +0x1c the edge's y and its steps from the y difference.

entries.name: Raster_FillRect
entries.description: (rect), C convention: fills the inclusive rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} with the brush at the installed clip block's +0x228 (the block 00098d64 points at). Brush mode 0 fills through g_RasterRoutines slot 2 (0009dedc), mode 6 remaps through slot 3 (0009dee0), and mode 4 draws the rect's outline with Raster_DrawLine under a temporary pen at +0x224; a colour whose top byte is 4 is read from the colour-ramp records at 0009a6f5. The rect moves by the block's translation when +0x208 is set and is clipped by its mode +0x204: 0 none, 1 the rect at +0x20c (00073dc4), otherwise each region of the list at +0, a rect region through 00073dc4 and a span region through 00073d8c and 00073b7c. ES2's Raster_FillRect (DBSIM 004865f8), statement for statement.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00053d9c, against ES2's Raster_FillRect

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: TSSolidPoly's vtable (0009b19a) slot +0x20. ES2's TSSolidPoly_Render (DBSIM 00474db4) without the .RMP: the chosen surface entries go to the brush colour 000b5f04 and PolyFill_LineColour as they are, brush mode 0, Poly_ProjectShapeVertices, Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane when needed, PolyFill_FillThenOutline(back).

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_Render
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: TSTexture4Poly's vtable (0009b1d2) slot +0x20. Picks the front or back value by ES2's -1 rule, takes that frame of the active bitmap bank (000bdb5e +8), and fills through the brush {7, 4, corners, the frame's bitmap header, table} at the render context's +0x22c (then PolyFill_FillBrush): the texture points are the frame's corners (0,0), (cols-1,0), (cols-1,rows-1), (0,rows-1) at 000b58d8 (Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithUV into 000b59dc when clipped); table is 0 while 000973f4 is 0, else 000973f0[(000973f4 - 1) * light / 255] with Light_ComputeShadeForFace's light, the normal negated for a back face.

entries.name: TSShadedPoly_Render
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: TSShadedPoly's vtable (0009b1fe) slot +0x20. As TSSolidPoly_Render (0005403c), after ORing (Light_ComputeShadeForFace & 0xff) << 16, the normal negated for a back face, into both colours, so a top byte of 4 picks that ramp entry from g_RasterColourRamps (0009a6f5). VSHELL's TSShadedPoly_Render (00423024) does the same; ES2's DBSIM one uses Palette_ShadeRampLookup and the .RMP.

entries.name: TSGouraudPoly_Render
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: TSGouraudPoly's vtable (0009b22a) slot +0x20. ES2's TSGouraudPoly_Render (DBSIM 004755c8): a Light_ComputeShadeForFace light per corner from the normal list (+0xe) and vertex list (+0xa), normals negated for a back face, into a stack array that 000b5f0c points at (through Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade when clipped), brush mode 1, PolyFill_FillThenOutline(back).

entries.name: ClassItem_RegisterBucket
entries.description: (count, entries) in stack order, callee-cleaned: when count is nonzero, appends {entries, count} to the bucket list at 000bd958 (8 bytes per bucket, entries first) and increments its count 000962b4. Light_ResetSystem (000632ec) registers g_TSObjectTypeRegistry with it. ES2's ClassItem_RegisterBucket (DBSIM 00479fac).

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadResource
entries.description: (mode, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: loads one class item. Points ClassItem_CurrentFrame (000b5adc) at a frame on its stack, reads the 8-byte type tag with 00055754, and for a tag other than -1 looks its handler up with 000554e2 and calls the handler's load function (+4) with (mode, stream); then runs 0005591d on the stream, restores the frame pointer and returns the item, or 0. ES2's ClassItem_LoadResource (DBSIM 0047a038), statement for statement.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 000551e0, against ES2's ClassItem_LoadResource

entries.name: ClassItem_StoreItem
entries.description: (item, mode, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: writes one class item. Points ClassItem_CurrentFrame at a frame on its stack and restores it on exit. When the item's body length (vtable +8) is 0 and the stream's slot +0x10 answers query 3 with 0, it makes a stream over the stream on its stack (00073f34(local, 0, 0, stream)), opens the item in it (000556cc) with the item's tag (vtable +4), calls the item's write slot (+0x14) with (mode, that stream), closes the item (00055860) and destroys the stream (00073fd0, flags 2); otherwise it runs the same open, write and close on the stream itself. ES2's ClassItem_StoreItem (DBSIM 0047a0a0).

entries.name: Arena_Alloc
entries.description: (arena, size) in stack order, callee-cleaned: bump-allocates from an arena {base +0, limit +4, cursor +8}: when arena is non-null and cursor + size is at most the limit it returns base + cursor and advances the cursor by size; otherwise it returns operator_new(size). ES2's Arena_Alloc (DBSIM 0047a1bc).

entries.name: ClassItem_PeekTypeTag
entries.description: (tag, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: saves the stream position (slot +8), reads the 8-byte type tag into tag (-1, 0 beforehand) through the read slot (+0x1c) and, when no handler is registered for it (through the thunk to 000554e4) and 000962b8 is set, copies it to 000bda48, reads the rest of the header (000962bc less 8 bytes) into 000bda50 and calls 00055568 through its thunk; seeks back (slot +0xc) unless the status (+0) is 2; returns status == 0. ES2's ClassItem_PeekTypeTag (DBSIM 0047a1fc).

entries.name: ClassItem_Skip
entries.description: (stream), callee-cleaned: reads a class item's 8-byte type tag and seeks past its body, the tag's second dword rounded up to an even length; returns status == 0. ES2's ClassItem_Skip (DBSIM 0047a2a8).

entries.name: ArenaStack_Push
entries.description: (cursor, limit, base) in stack order, callee-cleaned: increments the depth 000962c0, stores {base, limit, cursor} in the 12-byte entry at 000b5ae0 + depth * 12, points the current arena 000bd954 at it and returns base. ES2's ArenaStack_Push (DBSIM 0047a2f0).

entries.name: ArenaStack_Pop
entries.description: No arguments: decrements the depth 000962c0 and points the current arena 000bd954 at the entry below, or at null when the depth has gone negative (a signed test). ES2's ArenaStack_Pop (DBSIM 0047a368), whose test of the depth (TEST, JNC) can never take its null branch.

entries.name: ClassItem_ItemTotalSize
entries.description: (item), callee-cleaned: builds {tag = vtable +4, length = vtable +8} on its stack and returns 000555ec of it, or 0 when the length is 0. ES2's ClassItem_ItemTotalSize (DBSIM 0047a450).

entries.name: ClassItem_DebugPrintType
entries.description: (item, indent, unused) in stack order, callee-cleaned: prints indent spaces and 'Class type: %d:%d' with the high and low words of the item's tag (vtable +4) to stdout, then ' "%s"' with the name in the handler entry 000554e4 finds for the tag, when it finds one, and a newline. ES2's ClassItem_DebugPrintType (DBSIM 0047a488).

entries.name: Volume_Ctor
entries.description: Volume constructor, callee-cleaned (this): allocates 0x30 bytes through operator_new when this is null (0 if that fails), then clears the file stream +0, the buffered stream +4 and the arrays +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c. The class stores no vptr. ES2's Volume_Ctor (DBSIM 0047c894).

entries.name: Volume_Dtor
entries.description: Volume destructor (this, flags): returns at once for a null this; otherwise operator_delete on each of the arrays +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c that is set, deletes the buffered stream +4 and then the file stream +0 through their slot +4 with flags 3, and operator_delete on this when bit 0 of the flags is set. ES2's Volume_Dtor (DBSIM 0047c8bc).

entries.name: Volume_LoadVolume
entries.description: (bufferSize, mask, path) in stack order, callee-cleaned: opens path with FileRStream_Ctor and reads the 3-byte signature, which must equal 'VOL' (0009eb8c), a revision byte it ignores and the flags dword; when the flags share a bit with mask, wraps the file in BuffRStream_Ctor with a buffer of bufferSize bytes, 0x80 when smaller, and builds the volume with Volume_Ctor: file stream +0, buffered stream +4, path copied to +8, flags +0x20, then from the buffered stream the byte +0x1c, the directory count +0x1d, the directory-name block (word size, into +0x28, with +0x24 pointing at each name), the entry count +0x1e and the 0x12-byte entries (dword size, into +0x2c). Returns the volume, or 0 after Volume_Dtor(volume, 3) when the buffered stream's status is nonzero. A file that does not open, a wrong signature or flags sharing no bit with mask delete the file stream and return 0. ES2's Volume_LoadVolume (DBSIM 0047c9a4).

entries.name: Volume_FindEntry
entries.description: (volume, entry, path) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Path_Split's path into the static buffers 000bdcb6 (drive), 000bdcba (dir), 000bdcfc (name) and 000bdd06 (ext); when drive and dir are not empty, finds them among the directory names (+0x24, count +0x1d) with stricmp and returns 0 when none matches; then finds the first 0x12-byte entry (+0x2c, count +0x1e) whose directory index (+0xd) is that directory, or 0xff for none, and whose name equals name and ext with stricmp. On a hit it seeks the buffered stream +4 to the entry's offset (+0xe) through its slot +0xc, reads the entry's 9-byte prefix through its slot +0x1c, and fills entry: dword [0] the buffered stream, [2] and [4] the offset + 9, [5] the prefix's type byte and [6] its size dword; returns 1. Returns 0 when no entry matches. ES2's Volume_FindEntry (DBSIM 0047ccec).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Ctor
entries.description: VolumeGroup constructor, callee-cleaned, (this, dirFirst, dir, extension, mask) in stack order: allocates 0x29 bytes through operator_new when this is null (0 if that fails), clears the 10 volume pointers at +0 and the count byte +0x28, sets VolumeGroup_BufferSize (0009680c) to 0x400, then VolumeGroup_SetGroup with the same arguments, and returns this. ES2's VolumeGroup_Ctor (DBSIM 00467a98), which holds 0x1e volumes.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Dtor
entries.description: VolumeGroup destructor (this, flags): returns at once for a null this; otherwise Volume_Dtor (00055d50)(volume, 3) on each of the count (+0x28) volume pointers, and operator_delete when bit 0 of the flags is set. The class stores no vptr. ES2's VolumeGroup_Dtor (DBSIM 00467ae4).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize
entries.description: (size), callee-cleaned: stores max(size, 0x80) in VolumeGroup_BufferSize (0009680c). es2_xref finds one call, from main (Sim_Main (00059350)), with 0x200 just before main calls VolRStream_SetGroup; when that call makes the group, VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 over it before any volume is loaded. ES2's VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize (DBSIM 00467b30).

entries.name: Path_JoinSkipDrive

entries.description: (path), callee-cleaned: returns path + 2 when path[1] is ':', else path. ES2's Path_SkipDrive (DBSIM 00467bb8).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetGroup
entries.description: (group, dirFirst, dir, extension, mask) in stack order, callee-cleaned: walks the volumes by index and removes one whose flags (+0x20) share no bit with mask through VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume, then moves on past the volume shifted into its slot; returns when the group holds 10 volumes, then scans Str_Concat4's [dir]'vol\*'<extension> with findfirst and findnext twice, with dir the first time only when dirFirst is nonzero and the second time only when it is 0. Each file whose 'vol\<name>' equals no loaded volume's name (+8, through Path_SkipDrive) is added with VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, mask, Path_JoinSkipDrive('vol\<name>', that pass's dir)). The count is tested once, before the scans. ES2's VolumeGroup_SetGroup (DBSIM 00467bd4), which holds 0x1e volumes.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume
entries.description: (group, index): Volume_Dtor (00055d50)(volume, 3) on the volume at index, shifts the later pointers down one while they are set, decrements the count byte +0x28 and clears the freed last slot. ES2's VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume (DBSIM 00467e3c).

It does not test the count. ES2's VolumeGroup_AddVolume (DBSIM 00467e90).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_LoadVolume

entries.description: VolRStream destructor (this, flags), vtable slot +4: restores the vtable 0009683e, deletes the filters at +0x27 and +0x2b through their own slot +4 with flags 3, VolRStream_Close, Stream_BaseDtor(this, 0), and operator_delete when bit 0 of the flags is set. ES2's VolRStream_Dtor (DBSIM 00472e58).

entries.description: (stream, handle): VolRStream_Close, adopts the handle at +8 without owning it (+0x26 = 0) and probes it with lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR): status 0 on success, VolRStream_SetIoError on -1. ES2's VolRStream_SetFile (DBSIM 00472f30).

entries.name: VolRStream_Close
entries.description: (stream): closes the handle at +8 when the stream owns it (+0x26) and it is not -1, returning 0 with status 3 when close fails; passes the RLE filter +0x27 to RLERStream_Close (0007509c) and the LZH filter +0x2b to LZHRStream_Close (00074ccc) when set; clears +0xa, +0xe and +0x16, sets the handle to -1 and status 5, and returns 1. ES2's VolRStream_Close (DBSIM 00472f70).

entries.name: VolRStream_Open
entries.description: (stream, path): VolRStream_Close, clears +0xa, +0xe and +0x16, then open(path, 0) into the handle at +8. When that fails it looks the path up in the volume group g_VolumeGroup (00096838) through VolumeGroup_FindEntry (000566b8), which fills the entry fields from +0xa; with no group or no entry it sets status 1 and returns 0. By the entry's compression type at +0x1e it reads through: 2, the volume's stream itself (+0xe = +0xa); 7, the RLE filter at +0x27 (made by RLERStream_Ctor (00074f9c) on first use and attached by RLERStream_Open (00075068)); 9, the LZH filter at +0x2b (LZHRStream_Ctor (00074b8c), LZHRStream_Open (00074c70)). Then status 0 and +0x26 = 1, also for a volume entry, and returns 1 (MOV AL,1; the decompile drops both results). ES2's VolRStream_Open (DBSIM 00472fdc).

entries.name: VolRStream_SetGroup
entries.description: (a, b, c, d): makes the volume group g_VolumeGroup (00096838) through VolumeGroup_Ctor (00056180)(0, a, b, c, d) on first use, otherwise passes the same arguments to VolumeGroup_SetGroup (000562d8) on it. ES2's VolRStream_SetGroup (DBSIM 00473154).

entries.description: (): when the volume group g_VolumeGroup (00096838) is set, VolumeGroup_Dtor (000561d8)(group, 3) and clears g_VolumeGroup (00096838). Frameless (CMP, JE, the call, MOV, RET) after the padding at 00056a79; Ghidra had no function here. No caller found by es2_xref. ES2's VolRStream_DeleteGroup (DBSIM 004731e4).

entries.name: VolRStream_LoadVolume
entries.description: (path): passes the path to VolumeGroup_LoadVolume (00056620) on the volume group g_VolumeGroup (00096838). ES2's VolRStream_LoadVolume (DBSIM 00473210).

entries.description: (stream): filelength of the handle at +8 when there is one, otherwise the entry size +0x22 when an entry is open (+0xe), else 0. ES2's VolRStream_GetSize (DBSIM 00473228).

entries.name: VolRStream_GetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +8 (stream): lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR) for a file handle, the position in the entry (+0x16) when one is open, else 0. ES2's VolRStream_GetPosition (DBSIM 0047325c).

entries.name: VolRStream_SetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0xc (stream, position): a status of 2 is cleared first, and any other nonzero status returns 0. A file handle seeks with lseek(h, position, SEEK_SET), VolRStream_SetIoError on -1. An open entry stores the position at +0x16 and at +0x1a the absolute offset +0x12 + position, or, when the position is not below the size +0x22, the size itself with status 2; type 2 seeks the volume stream there, and types 7 and 9 reset their filter (RLERStream_Close (0007509c), LZHRStream_Close (00074ccc)), seek the volume stream to the entry's start, re-attach the filter (RLERStream_Open (00075068), LZHRStream_Open (00074c70)) and seek the filter to the position. Returns 1 otherwise. ES2's VolRStream_SetPosition (DBSIM 00473298).

entries.name: VolRStream_GetCapabilities
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0x10 (stream, query): for a file handle, query 0 answers 2 and queries 2 and 3 answer 1; for a volume entry, query 0 answers the compression type +0x1e, 2 and 3 answer 1 and 4 answers whether the type is not 2. Anything else answers 0. ES2's VolRStream_GetCapabilities (DBSIM 00473404).

entries.name: VolRStream_Flush

entries.name: VolRStream_SetIoError
entries.description: (stream): sets the status at +0 to 3 when errno (000973d3) is 0, otherwise 1, and returns 0. ES2's VolRStream_SetIoError (DBSIM 00473474).

entries.name: VolRStream_Write
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0x18: sets status 4 and returns 0. ES2's VolRStream_Write (DBSIM 00473498).

entries.name: VolRStream_Read
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0x1c (stream, buffer, count): 0 when the status is nonzero, 1 for a count of 0. A file handle reads through read(), VolRStream_SetIoError on -1 and status 2 with 0 returned on a short read. An entry first re-seeks (slot +0xc to +0x16) when the volume stream's position no longer equals +0x1a. A read running past the entry size +0x22 sets status 2, reads size - position + 1 bytes from the volume stream at +0xa itself, sets +0x16 to size + 1 and returns 0; any other reads count bytes through +0xe (the volume stream or the filter), adds count to +0x16 and returns 1. Both update +0x1a to the volume stream's position. The inner reads' results are not tested. ES2's VolRStream_Read (DBSIM 004734ac).

entries.name: Assert_Emit
entries.description: (message, line, file, condition, severity) in stack order, callee-cleaned (RET 0x14), switching on severity: 1 prints 'Assert: %d warning%s logged.' to the stream 0009e87c when the warning count 000b5b50 is not 0, the 's' left off for one; 2 passes the message to 00056f30; 3 counts a warning (000b5b50) and passes the line 00056e84 formats to 00056f30; 4 does the same without counting and also writes the line and a newline to 0009e87c; 5 writes 'Internal Error:' and a request to call Sierra customer support (000968ec), then the message, to 0009e87c; 6 passes 'Assert::break: Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Break' to 00056f30 and writes it to 0009e87c. Other severities do nothing. ES2's Assert_Emit (DBSIM 00479e18) is the counterpart.

entries.name: Assert_RunHooks
entries.description: (logger, severity), callee-cleaned: calls each hook on the list at 000b5b58 (+0 next, +4 the function) with the severity. ES2's Assert_RunHooks (DBSIM 00479b48) is the counterpart.

entries.name: Assert_Report
entries.description: (logger, message, line, file, condition, severity) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the member function Assert_Report(severity, condition, file, line, message) of ES2 (DBSIM 00479b6c), with the logger 000b5b54 as this. Severities 4, 5 and 6 are fatal: with 000b5bcc set it executes INT 3 and returns; otherwise it runs the hooks (Assert_RunHooks), emits the assert (Assert_Emit), emits severity 1 (the warning summary) and ends the program through __exit(1). Any other severity is only emitted.

The files built with it include data\results.dat, data\mission.var and data\mem.got.

entries.name: Sim_Main
entries.description: (a, b), main.cpp: the simulator's main. Mem_InitHeap(6000000), asserting at severity 5 (line 0xe3) when it gives 100000 bytes or fewer; 00058e30(b, a); copies to 000b5d9c, for 00056ecc, the ALT_DRIVE variable (taken as null unless 000b5bce is set) when PREFER_ALT is set and the string at 00096f6a otherwise; writes the heap size (4 bytes) to data\mem_got and an int16 0 to data\exit_cfg, asserting (lines 0xf1, 0xf9) when either does not open; 00058e74(b, a). With 000b5bc4 clear it closes the files at 000b5b82 and 000b5b7e, Mem_HeapOff, prints 'To play EarthSiege, type ES' and exits with 1. Otherwise Subsystem_RunPhase(0), VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize(0x200), VolRStream_SetGroup(PREFER_ALT set, ALT_DRIVE, 00096fde, 1), Subsystem_RunPhase(1); an assert (line 0x136) when the heap is under 0x26e8f0 bytes, g_LowMemory set when under 0x3c45b0; Sim_StartMission (0005a9dc), Subsystem_RunPhase(3); then each frame Subsystem_RunPhase(4), 00058574, 00063f40 while 000b5b76 is 0, leaving when 000b5bd2 or 00059700() is non-zero, else Cam_Update (000004b8)(000b5b8a), Sim_RenderFrame unless 000b5b76 and 000b5b92 are both set, 00059b40 and Subsystem_RunPhase(6). After the loop 0005b568, Mem_HeapOff, and with 000b5bc4 set and 000b5b9e clear, bit 0 of the byte 000b5b5c points at cleared.

entries.description: No arguments: the frame draw. ES2's Sim_RenderFrame (DBSIM 0045fb9c) has the same order with more steps.

Then builds the render context 000b5b6e with 00069a84(0), its origin +0x220/+0x224 (-160, -100) and +0x208 = 1 (its clip block's mode +0x204), stores the block at the display's +0x44, passes it to Raster_SetClipBlock while current, and installs the context with Raster_InstallRenderContext.

entries.description: (): the mission start Sim_Main (00059350) calls once. entries.description: (step, target, current) in stack order, callee-cleaned: moves the int16 *current toward target by step, stopping at target, and returns the error left (target - *current in magnitude), 0 once there. ES2's Math_RateLimitedMoveToward (DBSIM 004679d8).

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt
entries.description: (step, target, current) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward (0005e598) on an int32 *current: moves it toward target by step, stopping at target, and returns the error left in magnitude, 0 once there. No reference found by es2_xref. ES2's Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt (DBSIM 00467a24).

entries.name: Slew_Step
entries.description: (slew), callee-cleaned: advances a Slew one step and returns its position (+6, int16). With the error = target (+8) - position: when the error and the velocity (+0xa) do not have opposite signs and the error is inside the settle band (+4), the velocity becomes error >> shift (+0x10, arithmetic) and the acceleration (+0xc) 0; when they do not have opposite signs and the error is outside it, the acceleration moves toward the limit (+0) by the jerk (+2) and the velocity toward the top speed (+0xe) in the error's direction by the acceleration, both through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward; when they have opposite signs, the acceleration moves toward the limit the same way and the velocity steps toward the target by it, held at the error. The position then adds the velocity. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Slew_Ctor
entries.description: (slew, top speed, shift) in stack order, callee-cleaned: a Slew's constructor, allocating 0x12 bytes when slew is null. Stores the top speed (+0xe, uint16) and the shift (+0x10, byte), zeroes the velocity (+0xa) and the acceleration (+0xc), and derives the acceleration limit +0 = top speed >> shift and the jerk +2 = limit >> shift, each raised to 1 when 0, and the settle band +4 = top speed << shift. Leaves the position (+6) and target (+8) as they were. Returns slew. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Math_Q8Multiply
entries.description: (int a, int16 b), C convention: Q8 multiply rounded to nearest. IMUL of a by the sign-extended b, then SBB/XOR adds 0x80 when the product fits in 32 bits and 0xffffff7f when it does not, and SHRD EAX,EDX,8. ES2's Math_Q8Multiply (DBSIM 0047df94) truncates.

entries.name: Math_Q10Multiply
entries.description: (int a, int16 b), C convention: Q10 multiply rounded to nearest. Math_Q8Multiply's body with 0x200 (0xfffffdff when the product overflows 32 bits) and a shift of 10. ES2's Math_Q10Multiply (DBSIM 0047dfa4) truncates.

entries.name: Math_Q14Multiply
entries.description: (int a, int16 b), C convention: Q14 multiply rounded to nearest. Math_Q8Multiply's body with 0x2000 (0xffffdfff when the product overflows 32 bits) and a shift of 14. ES2's Math_Q14Multiply (DBSIM 0047dfb4) truncates.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToShortPoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out), C convention: transforms an int16 point by a 32-byte transform into an int32 result, rotation then translation, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding. Rank byte (+0x12) below 1: translation only; 1: rotates x and y only and passes z through; otherwise the full 3x3. ES2's Transform_ApplyToShortPoint (DBSIM 004800c8), whose decompile is the same after normalisation.

entries.name: Transform_RotationToEuler
entries.description: (rotation, out), C convention: out[0] = Math_AsinBam(m[5]); at a quarter turn either way out[1] = 0 and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[0], m[1]), otherwise out[1] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[8], -m[4]) and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[3], -m[2]). ES2's Transform_RotationToEuler (DBSIM 0047f894), whose decompile is the same after normalisation.

entries.name: Transform_Concat
entries.description: (a, b, out), C convention: composes two 32-byte transforms (nine Q14 int16 matrix entries, the rank byte +0x12, int translations +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c): out's rotation is a's times b's, each entry rounded (+0x2000 >> 14), and out's translation is a's rotated by b's rotation (64-bit, rounded) plus b's. A rank of 0 or less copies the other's rotation; two rank-1 operands (2x2) give a rank-1 result with +0x10 = 0x4000; anything else is rank 2. es2_naming.py diff finds it identical to ES2's Transform_Concat (DBSIM 0047f914).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0005ea08, against ES2's Transform_Concat

entries.name: Transform_RotatePoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out), C convention: Transform_ApplyToPoint without the translation -- the rotation alone on an int32 point, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates, with the rank-byte fast paths. ES2's Transform_RotatePoint (DBSIM 004801f8), whose decompile is the same after normalisation.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0005ef74, against ES2's Transform_RotatePoint

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: (euler, out), C convention: builds the Q14 rotation of a 32-byte transform from three int16 Euler angles, each trigonometry-table index being an angle shifted right 4 and rounded (SAR 4 then ADC 0, 15 times). ES2's BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 (DBSIM 0047eaac), whose decompile is the same after normalisation.

entries.name: Math_AsinBam
entries.description: (sine), C convention: the arcsine of a Q14 sine as a binary angle. Takes the magnitude, rounded to a multiple of 4 (SAR 2, ADC 0); below 0xe00 it reads the coarse table 00097634 at a further 8x step, rounded the same way, and from 0xe00 the fine table addressed from 00095db4 (its entries from 0xe00 on lie at 000979b4); the sign is restored at the end. ES2's Math_AsinBam (DBSIM 0047d940).

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out), C convention: transforms an int32 point by a 32-byte transform, rotation then translation, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates. Rank byte (+0x12) below 1: translation only; 1: rotates x and y only and passes z through; otherwise the full 3x3. ES2's Transform_ApplyToPoint (DBSIM 00480330), whose decompile is the same after normalisation.

entries.name: fprintf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `fprintf`, from `printf.c`: (stream, format, ...), C convention: returns vfprintf(stream, format, the address of the arguments after format). Symantec C++ 6.1's code for it matches here and at sprintf (0005f77c), as does its code for spawnl and spawnlp; the call to vfprintf settles it.

entries.name: vfprintf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `vfprintf`, from `printf.c`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 27 bytes from here.

entries.name: printf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `printf`, from `printf.c`: (format, ...), C convention: returns vprintf(format, the address of the arguments after format). Symantec C++ 6.1's code for printf, execl and execlp matches here; the call to vprintf settles it.

entries.name: vprintf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `vprintf`, from `printf.c`: (format, args), C convention: formats through _pformat (0005f7ca) with fputc onto stdout (_iob's second FILE, 0009e864), then calls fflush (000753e8) on stdout when bit 0x40 of its flags word (+0xc) is set, and returns the formatter's result.

entries.name: Printf_StoreChar
entries.description: (c, &cursor), C convention: the output routine vsprintf hands the formatter: stores c at *cursor, advances the cursor and returns c as an unsigned byte. printf.c's static helper between vprintf and sprintf; the library gives it no public name.

entries.name: sprintf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `sprintf`, from `printf.c`: (buffer, format, ...), C convention: returns vsprintf(buffer, format, the address of the arguments after format). Symantec C++ 6.1's code for it matches here and at fprintf (0005f6e0), as does its code for spawnl and spawnlp; the call to vsprintf settles it.

entries.name: vsprintf
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `vsprintf`, from `printf.c`: (buffer, format, args), C convention: formats through _pformat (0005f7ca) with Printf_StoreChar and a cursor on buffer, then stores a NUL at buffer plus the formatter's result, or at buffer itself when the result is negative.

entries.name: _pformat
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `_pformat`, from `printf.c`: (output, stream, format, args), C convention: the formatter vprintf, vfprintf and vsprintf share. Sends each character through output(c, stream) and returns the count sent, or -1 when output returns -1 or a conversion is not in its table. The flag characters are the table 00097ddc ('-', '+', ' ', '#', '0', '*'), digits are tested through the ctype table 0009edc5, and the conversions are the 18-entry table 00097e14 (s % c d i b o u p X x f F e E G g n), each with a handler address 0x48 bytes on; 6.1's printf.c reads F as a size modifier instead. Integer arguments come through getlong (0006010f).

entries.name: getlong
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `getlong`, from `printf.c`: (flags, &args) in stack order, callee-cleaned (Pascal): takes the next int from args and advances it; with flag 0x800 ('h') it sign-extends the low 16 bits, or zero-extends them when flag 0x200 (unsigned) is set too. _pformat's integer conversions call it. printf.c's static helper, the same as 6.1's 32-bit getlong.

entries.name: __DOSIGN
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `__DOSIGN`, from `printf.c`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 48 bytes from here.

entries.name: Mono_PrintfRow
entries.description: (format, row, ...), C convention: vsprintf into a 100-byte buffer and Mono_WriteText(buffer, row, 0), at the start of the row. The frame-rate meter's lines print with it.

entries.name: FrameRate_PrintRate
entries.description: (row, label, hundredths, whole) in stack order, callee-cleaned: prints label and a rate on a monochrome-screen row with Mono_PrintfRow, as "%s%2d.%02d fps." (the string 00097ee0 points to), or as "%s--.-- fps." (through 00097f04) when the rate is 999.99 or 0.00, the worst and best FrameRate_Update starts from.

entries.name: FrameRate_TimerTick
entries.description: No arguments, frameless: decrements FrameRate_Countdown (000b5e24) while it is non-zero. FrameRate_Update registers it with Timer_AddCallback (0006d289), count 1.

entries.name: FrameRate_GetFrameCount
entries.description: No arguments, frameless: returns FrameRate_FrameCount (000b5e28). 00000c84, in vcr.cpp, passes it to sprintf for its "Playback error. Frame #%ld" message.

entries.name: FrameRate_Update
entries.description: No arguments: the frame-rate meter, called once a frame. On its first call (FrameRate_TicksPerSecond FrameRate_TicksPerSecond (000b5e2c) is 0) it registers FrameRate_TimerTick with Timer_AddCallback (0006d289) at count 1, sets the ticks per second to 1000000 / Math_Q14Multiply(word +4 of the structure 000bdd0c points to, 0x35a1), loads FrameRate_Countdown (000b5e24) with 32000 and returns. Later calls take the ticks elapsed, e = 32000 - countdown, and reload it. e = 32000 prints "Current: Slower than %d fps." (00097f54) with 32000 / ticks per second on row 4. Otherwise, for e above the ticks per second, x = 10e / ticks per second and the rate shown is x / 10 and x % 10 as whole and hundredths, the seconds per frame in tenths printed as frames per second; for any other e, x = 100 * ticks per second / e, or 99999 when e is 0, and the rate is x / 100 and x % 100, which raises the best (FrameRate_Best (00097f58), whole then hundredths) when it is higher and neither 999 nor 99 hundredths, and lowers the worst (FrameRate_Worst (00097f5c)) when it is lower. It prints "Best:" on row 3 and "Worst:" on row 5 with FrameRate_PrintRate, then on row 4 "Current: Faster than %d fps." (00097f2c) with the ticks per second when x is 99999, or "Current:" and the rate. Each call after the first adds 1 to FrameRate_FrameCount (000b5e28) and prints "Frame # %d" on row 1. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: fclose
entries.description: The runtime's fclose (stream), C convention: -1 for a null stream. For one open in any mode (flags +0xc & 0x83) it flushes it with fflush unless flag 4 (unbuffered) is set, and closes the handle +0x10; when the stream's temporary-file number at 000bdbe6[(stream - _iob) / 0x18] is set it removes the file named by that number in decimal (ltoa, remove) and clears it; then File_FreeBuffer and a memset of the FILE's 0x18 bytes. Returns the or of fflush's and close's results.

entries.name: fwrite
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `fwrite`, from `fread.c`: (buffer, size, count, stream), C convention: writes size * count bytes and returns the number of whole items written. A stream with flag 0x100 (+0xc) takes them one fputc at a time; a buffered one (flag 4 clear) copies them into its buffer (pointer +0, room +4) with memmove, calling 00075fd5 with the byte when the room is 0; an unbuffered one in write mode (flags & 0x32 == 2, a read-write stream with 0x80 switched to it first) takes one write to its handle (+0x10), setting the error flag 0x20 on a short count, and otherwise writes nothing.

entries.name: fopen
entries.description: The runtime's fopen (name, mode), C convention: takes the first FILE of _iob whose flags +0xc & 0x83 are clear, up to the one ending at 0009eb57, and returns 000761dc(stream, mode, name); with none free it sets errno to 4 and returns 0.

entries.name: Str_ReplaceFirst
entries.description: (replace, find, s) in stack order, callee-cleaned: replaces the first occurrence of the character find in s with replace (strchr) and returns s. ES2's Str_ReplaceFirst (DBSIM 00492a5c).

entries.name: Path_WithExtension
entries.description: (extension, path) in stack order, callee-cleaned: copies path into the static buffer 000b5e30, cuts it at the first '.' (Str_ReplaceFirst), appends '.' and extension, and returns the buffer. ES2's Path_WithExtension (DBSIM 00492a84).

entries.name: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName
entries.description: (folder, name) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the resource path folder\name.folder. Path_WithExtension(name, folder), then copies folder into the static buffer 000b5e50, appends '\' and the Path_WithExtension result, and returns the buffer. ES2's ResourcePath_BuildFolderName (DBSIM 00492ae0).

entries.name: NameList_Split
entries.description: (out, buffer) in stack order, callee-cleaned: walks the NUL-terminated names in buffer until one starts with a '\n' byte, storing each name's address in out when out is non-null, and returns the count. ES2's NameList_Split (DBSIM 00492b40).

entries.name: VolFile_GetSize
entries.description: (path), callee-cleaned: opens path as a VolRStream and returns VolRStream_GetSize, or 0 when the stream's status word (+0) is set after the open. ES2's VolFile_GetSize (DBSIM 00492b78), which reads the status through Stream_GetStatus.

entries.name: LoadNameList
entries.description: (stride, capacity, mod mask, name) in stack order, callee-cleaned: loads the type-name list nam\<name>.NAM and the mod lists nam\<name>1.NAM to nam\<name>8.NAM into a table of capacity pointers (operator new, zeroed) and returns it. List k from 1 to 8 is read only when bit k-1 of the mask is set. Each file read is sized with VolFile_GetSize, all of them are read whole into one buffer, and NameList_Split stores each file's names: the base list's from entry 0, and list k's from entry capacity - 8 * stride + (k - 1) * stride. Mechs_InitAllTypes calls it with ('mechs', 0x60 entries, stride 10) and FlyerTypes_LoadAll (0001c770) with ('flyers', 0x52, 10), both with mask 0. ES2's LoadNameList (DBSIM 00492bf4) takes (name, capacity) and loads the base list only.

entries.name: MechMods_Probe
entries.description: No arguments: for n from 1 to 8 opens MECMODn.DYN (00097f84, mode "rb") with fopen and closes it, setting bit n-1 of MechMods_Present (000b5e6e) for each that opens. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: memmove

entries.name: fread
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `fread`, from `fread.c`: (buffer, size, count, stream), C convention: reads up to size * count bytes and returns the number of whole items read. A stream with flag 0x100 (+0xc) gives them one fgetc at a time; a buffered one (flag 4 clear) copies them out of its buffer (pointer +0, count +4) with memmove, refilling it through 00076106 when it is empty; an unbuffered one in read mode (flags & 0x31 == 1, a read-write stream with 0x80 switched to it first) calls 00075ecc and takes one read from its handle (+0x10), setting the end-of-file flag 0x10 when it returns 0 and the error flag 0x20 when it fails.

entries.name: memset
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `memset`, from `strings.ASM`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 49 bytes from here.

entries.name: X32_LockRegion
entries.description: (offset, selector, size), C convention: INT 21h AX=252Bh with BX=0501h, ES:ECX the region's far address and EDX its size; returns 0, or -1 when the call sets the carry. AX=252Bh is the Phar Lap memory-region call the extender provides, whose subfunction BH=5 locks pages and BH=6 unlocks them. 0006f971 locks a list of code and data ranges with it, and 0006fb96 unlocks the same ranges with X32_UnlockRegion.

entries.name: X32_UnlockRegion
entries.description: (offset, selector, size), C convention: loads BX=0601h and jumps into X32_LockRegion's INT 21h AX=252Bh body: the Phar Lap memory-region call's unlock subfunction (BH=6).

entries.name: maybe_X32_AllocSelector
entries.description: (linear), C convention: INT 21h AX=3501h, then AX=3503h with ECX = linear and AX=3505h with ECX = 0xffffffff on the selector it returned in BX; returns EAX = 0 and EDX = that selector. When 3503h or 3505h fails it frees the selector (AX=3502h) and returns -1; when 3501h fails it returns linear with DX the data selector 0009003a. The service names (allocate, free, set base, set limit) are inferred; compiler.md lists the AX=35xxh calls as Open.

entries.name: maybe_X32_FreeSelector
entries.description: (offset, selector), C convention: returns -1 for the data selector 0009003a; otherwise loads 0 into whichever of ES, FS and GS holds the selector, calls INT 21h AX=3502h and returns 0, or -1 on carry. offset is not read. maybe_X32_AllocSelector frees through the same call.

entries.name: __vec_new
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `__vec_new`, from `vecnew.cpp`: (ctor, count, size, p) in stack order, callee-cleaned; 6.1's library declares it (p, size, count, ctor). Stores count in the first dword, calls ctor (when non-null) on each element from the next dword at size intervals, and returns the address after the count.

When p is non-null: when dtor is non-null, calls dtor(element, 2) on each element, last first, their count read from the dword before p; then calls operator_delete(p - 4) when flags bit 0 is set.

When p and dtor are both non-null it calls dtor(element, 2) on each of the count elements at size intervals from p, the last first; 2 is DTORmostderived.

entries.description: (stream), callee-cleaned: when the stream owns its buffer (flags +0xc bit 3) frees the buffer +8 if set and clears the bit; then zeroes the pointer +0, the buffer +8, the size +0x14 and the count +4. fclose calls it.

entries.name: maybe_MonoCrtc_HideCursor
entries.description: No arguments, frameless, keeps EDX: writes 0xf to the monochrome CRTC's register 0xa (cursor start scan line; index port 3b4, data 3b5), below the cursor end that mode 7's BIOS cursor uses (0xc), which hides it on a 6845.

entries.name: maybe_MonoCrtc_ShowCursor
entries.description: No arguments, frameless, keeps EDX: writes 0xb to the monochrome CRTC's register 0xa (cursor start scan line; index port 3b4, data 3b5), mode 7's BIOS cursor start.

entries.name: Crtc_DetectDualDisplay
entries.description: No arguments, keeps ECX and EDX: returns 1 when Crtc_Probe (00076377) answers at both 3b4, the monochrome adapter's CRTC index port, and 3d4, the colour adapter's; otherwise 0. MonoScreen_Ctor calls it.

entries.name: Crtc_Probe
entries.description: Register argument DX = a CRTC index port: reads the cursor-location registers 0xe and 0xf through the data port DX+1, writes 4 and 0xa to them, reads both back, restores the saved values through Crtc_RestoreCursorLocation (000763d4) and returns DX = 1 when both read back as written, else DX = 0.

entries.name: Crtc_RestoreCursorLocation
entries.description: Register argument DX = a CRTC data port, with two words its caller pushed under the return address, the saved register 0xf value on top and 0xe below: writes them back to registers 0xf and 0xe through the index port DX-1 and returns with both popped. Crtc_Probe's exit.

entries.name: Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms
entries.description: (a, b, q, out), C convention: blends two 12-byte keyframe records by the Q10 factor q, an int16: the three angles along the shortest arc, the three translations as a truncating lerp. ES2's Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms (DBSIM 00492600), which takes q as an int.

entries.description: (script): allocates the 0x1c1-byte .TTM script when given none (returning 0 when that fails); constructs twelve 0x18-byte objects at +0x58 with __vec_ctor; sets the dwords +0x19d and +0x1a5 to 0 and +0x1ad to 4, and zeroes +0x1b5, +0x1b9 and +0x1bd.

ES1GO's GLRectangleRegion_Ctor (00046c6c) with the simulator's vtables. es2_xref finds its padding entry 0007987f stored at 000797db, in TtmScript_Ctor (000797ac), for the script's twelve regions.

ES1GO's GLRectangleRegion_Dtor (00046dc4) with the simulator's vtables. es2_xref finds it at 0009f2ea, the +0x1c slot of the vtable 0009f2ce.

entries.name: TtmScript_Dtor
entries.description: (script, flags): returns at once for a null script; otherwise calls TtmScript_Free (00079f68)(script) through its padding entry, destroys the twelve objects at +0x58 with __vec_dtor, and deletes the script when bit 0 of the flags is set.

entries.name: TtmScript_Run
entries.description: (script, ticks) in stack order, callee-cleaned: notes the default render context 0009f248 and, when the script's +0x1bd is not 0, sets 0009f248 to it and installs it with Raster_InstallRenderContext. Subtracts ticks from the wait +0x182. While it is above 0: unless the mode dword +0xe is 2, runs the page byte +1 with TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58). Otherwise: when the byte +0x18a is 1 subtracts ticks from +0x186 and, below 0, reloads it from +0x188 and calls TtmScript_CyclePalette (00079d90); reloads the wait from +0x184; then through the table 0009f2f4 by mode: 0 runs the page, then takes the page +0x178 when it is not -1 (setting it to -1) or else adds 1 to the page and clears the byte +0x12, and when the page has reached the count byte +0 resets the script with TtmScript_Reset (0007ca44) and sets the mode to 0 when the loop dword +0x13 is 1, to 2 otherwise; 1 runs the page; 3 resets and sets the mode as at the end; 2 does nothing. Finally restores and installs the noted context and returns 1. es2_xref finds one call, from Ttm_RunAll (000695e0).

entries.name: TtmScript_BuildPath
entries.description: (script, name): rewrites the first .SCR in name to .DBM, .BMP to .DBA and .PAL to .DPL (Str_FindBoyerMoore, strncpy of 4), and returns the buffer 000bbbf0 holding the prefix 0009f254, when there is one, followed by the name. ES1GO's also upper-cases the name and rewrites .RAW.

entries.name: TtmScript_FixRect
entries.description: (script, rect): with the display object 0009f24c's +0x38 set to the low byte of its +0x3c and its +0x3c to 0009f250, Ttm_ManagerCtor's a (each store also copied to 00098dd6 or 00098dda and passed to the routine at 0009df14 or 0009df18 when the display is 000bdd28), copies a type-0 region of rect at (0, 0) with Region_CopyBetweenPages (00066914), passes rect to DirtyBox_Add (0008398c) with 0 (in stack order x0, y0, x1, y1, 0), then puts back the low bytes of the two fields. es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58), three, and TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0007c01c).

entries.name: TtmScript_CyclePalette
entries.description: (script): ES1GO's TtmScript_CyclePalette (000472d0) at the simulator's offsets: rotates by one place each of the three six-byte ranges at +0x18b whose direction (+0x18f, +0x195, +0x19b) is not 0 in the palette of the slot table +0x21 selected by +0x25, then uploads it with Palette_UploadWhole. es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_Run (00079a14).

entries.description: (script): resets the script with TtmScript_Reset (0007ca44) through its padding entry, then deletes the unpacked script +6, the page table +2 and the slot tables +0x21 and +0x17 when set. ES1GO's TtmScript_Free (000474bd) also destroys a sound object. es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_Dtor, through the padding entry 00079f67.

entries.description: (script, source, count): copies count bytes from source, or with a count of 0 the bytes up to its NUL, at most 100 either way, into the buffer 000bbc18, adds a NUL and returns the buffer. ES1GO's TtmScript_CopyArgBytes (0004759d) with the simulator's buffer.

The opcodes and the 2,034 bytes of strings from 0009f322 are the same as ES1GO's Ttm_TokenName (00047618)'s. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: TtmScript_Load
entries.description: (script, a, b, name) in stack order, callee-cleaned: loads a .TTM. Opens TtmScript_BuildPath (00079b54)'s path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath and returns 3 when its status is not 0; TtmScript_FindTag (0007cba4) PAG:, reads the size dword and one byte, the page count's low byte; TT3:, reads the size dword and the method byte, returning 2 unless it is 1, then the unpacked length; allocates it at +6 (1 when that fails) and reads it through an RLERStream on the file stream, returning 1 when the file stream's status is then not 0. Closes the file stream, stores the page count byte at +0, count + 1 dwords at +2, +6 + length - 1 at +0xa, 0x18 bytes at +0x21 and +0x17, freeing them and returning 1 when one fails; indexes the pages with TtmScript_IndexPages (0007a940) through its padding entry; zeroes the two blocks and the fields, stores a at +0xe and b at +0x13, 0xff at the bytes +0x178 and +0x179, 10 at the dwords +0x1a1, +0x1a9 and +0x1b1; destroys the streams (RLERStream_DtorCopy (0007a914)'s vtable 0009ff16, VolRStream_Dtor) and returns the index result, 0 or 2. ES1GO's TtmScript_Load does not test the open or the method byte and reads the page count as a word. es2_xref finds one call, from Ttm_Open.

entries.name: RLERStream_DtorCopy
entries.description: (stream, flags): RLERStream_Dtor's code with the TTM module's copy of RLERStream's vtable, 0009ff16: returns at once for a null stream; otherwise stores that vtable, Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), and operator_delete when bit 0 of the flags is set.

entries.name: TtmScript_IndexPages
entries.description: (script): ES1GO's TtmScript_IndexPages over this script's fields (page count byte +0, page table +2, script +6, last byte +0xa): stores each page's start and steps over commands to the step past an opcode 0x0ff0, returning 2 when the position reaches +0xa at a page's start or after a command, or on low bits 8-14, and 0 with every page found. Strings are skipped with TtmScript_SkipString (00079fb0).

entries.name: TtmScript_RunPage
entries.description: (script, page) in stack order, callee-cleaned: ES1GO's TtmScript_RunPage (00048218) at the simulator's offsets, running the page from the page table +2 to its 0x0ff0 and returning 1, with these differences. Its call offsets (depth +0x17a, x +0x17c, y +0x17e) skip the opcodes of the table 0009ffac (targets 0009ffbc, JMP 0007ad1d). It steps over every opcode 0xc000-0xcfff; hands 0xa000-0xafff to TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0007c01c), returning 0 when that returns 0; finds the rest in the 29 opcodes at 0009ffcc (targets 000a0040, JMP 0007adea), the shell's 30 less 0x5005, and steps over any other. Point lists go through TtmScript_CopyArgBytes (00079fdc). Loads, frees, palette selects, 0x0020, 0x4204, 0x4214, 0x2402, 0x0400, 0xf01f and 0x4124 act while the wait +0x182 is 0 or less; 0x1021 and 0x2022 act once per page through the byte +0x12, 0x2022 as min + labs(rand (0007cd28)() % (max - min)); 0x4114 acts on every run. Palettes are uploaded with Palette_UploadWhole on select and load; bitmap arrays are destroyed with GLBitmapArray_Dtor (000673c8)(array, 3); 0xf01f's bitmap is loaded with ClassItem_LoadResource and its rect fixed with TtmScript_FixRect (00079c38). The fades work on a stack palette set up with GLPalette_Assign (0007bfdc), scale colours a1 to a2 toward black with Palette_ScaleRange (0007cc24) by the step 6 - a4, copy the full screen with Region_CopyBetweenPages (00066914) and destroy the copy with GLPalette_Dtor (00069258). Labels are found with TtmScript_FindLabel (00079ef4). es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_Run (00079a14), three, and from its own 0x3003 and 0x3303 cases, through the padding entry 0007aa57.

entries.name: GLPalette_Assign
entries.description: (palette, source): copies the words +4, +6, +0xc, +0xe and the dwords +8 (the colours) and +0x10 from source, leaving the vtable. ES1GO's GLPalette_Assign (0004a08c). es2_xref finds calls from the two fade cases of TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58).

entries.name: TtmScript_RunDrawCommand
entries.description: (script, string, seven arguments, opcode) in stack order, callee-cleaned: ES1GO's TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0004a213) at the simulator's offsets: matches the opcode against the shell's 22 at 000a00b4 (targets 000a010c, JMP 0007c040) and returns 1 whether or not one matches. The pen +0x228 and fill +0x22c of the default render context 0009f248 are set to the brushes +0x19d, +0x1a5 and +0x1ad. Each draw but 0xa601 passes its box to DirtyBox_Add (0008398c) with 1; the ellipses draw with Raster_DrawEllipse (000831f4) and the sized brush with Bitmap_BlitScaled (00067178); one case serves the twelve bitmap draws, testing the opcode's low four bits, and adds the dwords +0x1b5 and +0x1b9 to the position. 0xa601, while the wait +0x182 is 0 or less, puts the selected region's saved pixels back with Region_Restore at (0, 0) and passes the region's rect to TtmScript_FixRect (00079c38). es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58), through the padding entry 0007c01b.

entries.name: TtmScript_Reset
entries.description: (script): destroys the six palettes of the slot table +0x21 through their +0x1c slot with 3 and the six bitmap arrays of +0x17 with GLBitmapArray_Dtor (000673c8)(array, 3), deletes the twelve saved-pixel buffers at +0x28, zeroing every slot; zeroes the cycling directions +0x18f, +0x195 and +0x19b; sets the mode dword +0xe to 2, the page byte +1 and the palette slot +0x25 to 0, the word +0x178 to -1, the words +0x17a to +0x188 and the byte +0x18a to 0, and the brush colours +0x1a1, +0x1a9 and +0x1b1 to 10. ES1GO's TtmScript_Reset (0004b3c6) at the simulator's offsets; this one leaves the byte +0x12. es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_Run (00079a14), two, and TtmScript_Free (00079f68), through the padding entry 0007ca43.

entries.name: TtmScript_FindTag
entries.description: (script, tag, stream): ES1GO's Stream_FindTag search with the script first, unused: notes the stream's position (slot +8) and reads a byte at a time (slot +0x1c) until the NUL-terminated tag has matched or a read fails; a matching byte advances through the tag, a byte that does not match restarts at the tag's first byte without being tested against it; on a failure seeks (slot +0xc) back. Returns whether the whole tag matched, the stream then just past it.

entries.name: Palette_ScaleRange

entries.name: LZHuffman_Ctor
entries.description: LZHuffman constructor, callee-cleaned (this): allocates 0x16 bytes through operator_new when this is null (0 if that fails), then through operator_new the frequency table +4 (0x4e8 bytes), the parent links +8 (0x75a) and the child links +0xc (0x4e6), LZHUF's sizes for 314 symbols and a 627-node tree. The class stores no vptr. ES2's LZHuffman_Ctor (DBSIM 0047bb50).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Dtor
entries.description: LZHuffman destructor (this, flags): returns at once for a null this; otherwise operator_delete on the tables +4, +8 and +0xc, and on this when bit 0 of the flags is set. ES2's LZHuffman_Dtor (DBSIM 0047bb90).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Start
entries.description: (coder, source): attaches the source at +0, clears the bit-input state +0x10..+0x15, and builds LZHUF's initial tree: 314 (0x13a) leaves of frequency 1 (frequencies +4) whose child links (+0xc) are 0x273 + i and parent links (+8, from +0x4e6) their node, then the internal nodes 0x13a..0x272 each summing a pair, the sentinel frequency 0xffff at node 0x273 and parent 0 for the root 0x272. LZHUF's StartHuff. ES2's LZHuffman_Start (DBSIM 0047bbd0).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodeChar
entries.description: (coder, c): walks the parent links (+8, leaf c's at +0x4e6) up to the root 0x272, shifting each node's low bit into the code from the top, then LZHuffman_PutCode(coder, code, bit count) and LZHuffman_Update(coder, c). LZHUF's EncodeChar. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodeChar (DBSIM 0047bc80).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodePosition
entries.description: (coder, position): LZHuffman_PutCode with the code 000a7cd0[position >> 6] << 8 and the length 000a7c90[position >> 6] (LZHUF's p_code and p_len), then the low six bits << 10 in 6 bits. LZHUF's EncodePosition. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodePosition (DBSIM 0047bcd4).

entries.name: LZHuffman_DecodeChar
entries.description: (coder): walks the child links (+0xc) from the root (+0x4e4) one LZHuffman_GetBit at a time until a leaf (>= 0x273), LZHuffman_Update's it and returns leaf - 0x273. LZHUF's DecodeChar. ES2's LZHuffman_DecodeChar (DBSIM 0047bd18).

entries.name: LZHuffman_DecodePosition
entries.description: (coder): reads a byte with LZHuffman_GetByte, takes the upper six bits from 000a7d10 and the bit count from 000a7e10 (LZHUF's d_code and d_len), shifts count - 2 more bits from LZHuffman_GetBit into the byte from below and returns its low six bits | upper << 6, a 12-bit position. LZHUF's DecodePosition. ES2's LZHuffman_DecodePosition (DBSIM 0047bd68).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodeEnd
entries.description: (coder): writes the top byte of the bit buffer (+0x13) when bits are pending (+0x15), then a zero byte, each through the stream's slot +0x18. LZHUF's EncodeEnd with a trailing 0. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodeEnd (DBSIM 0047bdbc).

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetBit
entries.description: (coder): while the bit count +0x12 is below 9, reads a byte through the source's slot +0x1c (0 when the read fails), ORs it into the 16-bit buffer +0x10 below the bits held and adds 8 to the count; then shifts out and returns the top bit. LZHUF's GetBit. ES2's LZHuffman_GetBit (DBSIM 0047bdec).

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetByte
entries.description: (coder): LZHuffman_GetBit's refill, then shifts out and returns the top 8 bits. LZHUF's GetByte. ES2's LZHuffman_GetByte (DBSIM 0047be4c).

entries.name: LZHuffman_PutCode
entries.description: (coder, code, length) in stack order: ORs the code, shifted right by the pending bit count +0x15, into the output buffer +0x13 and adds length to the count; at 8 bits or more writes the buffer's top byte through the stream's slot +0x18, and when 8 still remain its low byte too and keeps code << (length - count). LZHUF's Putcode. ES2's LZHuffman_PutCode (DBSIM 0047beac).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Reconstruct
entries.description: (coder): rebuilds the adaptive Huffman tree: gathers the leaves (child link above 0x272) to the front with their frequencies (+4) halved, rounding up, rebuilds the internal nodes 0x13a..0x272 in frequency order with memmove, and relinks the parents (+8). LZHUF's reconst. ES2's LZHuffman_Reconstruct (DBSIM 0047bf20).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Update
entries.description: (coder, c): LZHuffman_Reconstruct when the root frequency (+4 at 0x4e4) is 0x8000, then increments the frequencies from leaf c up to the root, swapping a node past its lower-frequency successors to keep the order, with their child and parent links. LZHUF's update. ES2's LZHuffman_Update (DBSIM 0047c054).

entries.name: Emu8000_WriteWord
entries.description: (value, register) in stack order, callee-cleaned: writes a word to a Sound Blaster AWE32 EMU8000 register with interrupts off (restored only when they were on). The register code's bits 0-4 (channel) and bits 12-14 (moved to bits 5-7) go to the pointer port, the Data0 port 000acd42 + 0x802; the value goes to Data0 + (code & 0xc00), plus 2 when bit 9 is set. 00084516 sets Data0 to the base it is given, adding 0x400 to one below 0x300 (0x220 becomes 0x620).

entries.name: Emu8000_WriteDword
entries.description: (value, register) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Emu8000_WriteWord for a 32-bit register: the low word to the selected data port and the high word to that port + 2.

entries.name: Emu8000_ReadDword
entries.description: (register), callee-cleaned: Emu8000_ReadWord for a 32-bit register: the low word from the selected data port, the high word from that port + 2.

entries.name: VGA8_BlitBitmap
entries.description: (header, point, clip, flags) in stack order: the VGA_8 driver's bitmap blit, its table's +0x68: clips the bitmap's rows (+0) and columns (+2) against clip when clip is non-null, mirrors by flags bits 1 and 2, and writes the bytes to display memory through the sequencer's map mask (ports 3c4/3c5) a plane at a time. With header byte +5's bit 4 set every byte is written; with it clear a 0 byte is skipped, leaving the pixel.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM disassembly at 0008b9a8 (head, clip, flag tests and copy loops)

entries.name: VGA8_BlitBitmapClipped
entries.description: (header, point, clip, flags), C convention: the VGA_8 driver's clipped blit, its table's +0x70 (0009df44): with clip non-null trims the bitmap's columns and rows to the rect clip (returning when nothing is left), picks the start and the row and column steps by flags bits 1 and 2, and draws each destination row with VGA8_BlitClippedRow, a plane at a time. With header byte +5's bit 4 set every byte is written; with it clear a 0 byte is skipped (OR AL,AL / JZ at 0008c58b).

entries.name: VGA8_BlitClippedRow
entries.description: A block of VGA8_BlitBitmapClipped, near-called with its frame (EBP) per destination row ([EBP-0x38]): in clip mode +0x204 2 clips the row to each region of the clip block's list in turn, a type-0 rect or a type-2 span region, passing over regions of other types; otherwise draws it once. For each of the four planes writes that plane's pixels of the row, every byte when header bit 4 is set, and only the non-zero ones when it is clear.

entries.name: BMP8_BlitBitmap
entries.description: The BMP_8 driver's bitmap blit, its table's +0x68: copies the bitmap's rows into the canvas bitmap, by flag bits 1 and 2 in one of four orders (cases 0-3). With header byte +5's bit 4 set each row goes by REP MOVSD/MOVSB, or byte by byte when mirrored; with it clear each 0 byte is skipped, leaving the destination. The clipped blit 0008dc3c calls it.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM disassembly at 0008d700 (the case blocks and copy loops)
